3. I am not self-employed in 2024 and do not have any Schedule C or Schedule F activity.
4. I have detailed records of the square footage of the office relative to the home, as well as direct and indirect expenses (rent, utilities, internet, etc.).

rounds.response: Short answer: generally no — for tax years 2018–2025 the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act suspended the miscellaneous itemized deduction for unreimbursed employee business expenses, so a typical W‑2 employee cannot claim a home‑office deduction on Form 1040 in 2024. Very narrow exceptions exist (for example, taxpayers treated as statutory employees who report on Schedule C, and certain special categories with separate Code treatment such as qualified performing artists, some reservists, and fee‑basis government officials), but those exceptions are uncommon and each has detailed statutory tests. Conservatively stated, if you are an ordinary W‑2 employee with no Schedule C/statutory‑employee status, your employer’s written telework requirement and exclusive use do not create a federal home‑office deduction for 2024; if you believe one of the narrow exceptions might apply, consider getting a tax professional to review the specific facts and documentation.
